framework_version: CIS Fortinet FortiGate Benchmark (control intent; clause numbers not asserted)
source_note: The conditions in this pack are byte-for-byte the conditions in the Cisco IOS and Junos packs, because all three read the same vendor-neutral baseline fields - that is what the baseline is for. What is FortiOS-specific is the remediation, which is FortiOS CLI. Clause numbers are deliberately NOT asserted: the control intent follows the CIS Fortinet FortiGate Benchmark, but the exact clause numbering could not be verified against a licensed copy, and inventing one would be worse than omitting it. Map each rule to its clause from your own copy before citing this output in a formal audit.

rules.title: Authenticate administrators against a centralised server
rules.description: Administrative logins should be authenticated by RADIUS or TACACS+ so that accounts, password policy and revocation are managed in one place rather than per device.
rules.rationale: A local-only account survives an operator leaving the organisation and leaves no central record of who logged in.

remediation.summary: Define a RADIUS or TACACS+ server and point an administrator account at it.

rules.notes: FortiOS needs both halves: a server under 'config user', and an account with 'set remote-auth enable'. Either alone leaves administrative logins local.

rules.title: Permit no cleartext administrative access in 'set allowaccess'
rules.description: No interface should include telnet in its allowaccess list. SSH should be the only interactive administrative transport the device offers.
rules.rationale: Telnet carries the administrator password across the network in the clear, and allowaccess is evaluated per interface, so one WAN-facing interface is enough to expose it.

remediation.summary: Rewrite allowaccess on every interface, naming only the protocols that interface must serve.

rules.notes: 'set allowaccess' replaces the whole list; there is no incremental form. Restate every protocol the interface should keep.

rules.title: Set 'admintimeout' to 10 minutes or less
rules.description: An administrative session should be closed after a bounded period of inactivity, and must not be configured never to time out.
rules.rationale: An unattended session left open on an administrator's workstation is an authenticated session anyone at that desk can use.

remediation.summary: Set the administrative idle timeout to 10 minutes.

rules.notes: 'admintimeout' is expressed in minutes on the device; the baseline stores it in seconds.

rules.title: Store every administrator password as a hash
rules.description: Every administrator account should carry a password, and no password should be written into the configuration in recoverable form.
rules.rationale: A configuration file is copied to backup servers, ticket systems and laptops; a credential written in the clear is disclosed everywhere it travels.

remediation.summary: Set the password through the CLI so FortiOS stores and writes back only the hash.
cli: # FortiOS writes the credential back as: set password ENC <hash>

rules.notes: The 'ENC' keyword in front of a stored password is what marks it hashed. A 'set password' statement without it is a cleartext credential.

rules.title: Unset the default 'public' and 'private' SNMP communities
rules.description: No reachable SNMP v1/v2c community should use a default name.
rules.rationale: Default community names are the first thing an internet-wide scan tries, and a v2c community is a cleartext password that discloses the device's whole configuration and topology.

remediation.summary: Delete the default community and replace it with a non-default name limited to the management network.

rules.title: Enforce SSH protocol version 2
rules.description: The device must not accept SSH protocol version 1.
rules.rationale: SSHv1 has known integrity and session-key weaknesses and offers no benefit over v2.

remediation.summary: Disable SSHv1 compatibility explicitly, so the configuration states the enforced version.

rules.notes: 'admin-ssh-v1' exists in FortiOS 6.x and was removed in 7.x, which speaks v2 only. A configuration that states neither leaves the enforced version to a release default, which is reported as NEEDS_REVIEW rather than guessed.

rules.title: Do not serve the administrative GUI over plain HTTP
rules.description: No interface should include http in its allowaccess list.
rules.rationale: The FortiOS GUI authenticates with an administrator password; served over HTTP that password and the session cookie cross the network in the clear.

remediation.summary: Remove http from allowaccess and redirect administrative GUI traffic to HTTPS.

rules.title: Configure a log destination
rules.description: The device should ship logs to a syslog server, retain them on box, or both — and the destination must be enabled, not merely configured.
rules.rationale: Logs held only on the device are lost in exactly the incident that makes them worth reading.

remediation.summary: Enable a remote syslog server, and keep an on-box store as well.

rules.notes: Each log destination carries its own 'set status'. A server configured with 'set status disable' ships nothing and does not satisfy this control.

rules.title: Restrict every administrator account with a trusthost
rules.description: Every account under 'config system admin' should be limited to the source addresses administration is performed from.
rules.rationale: FortiOS has no equivalent of a management access-list on the login line: until a trusthost narrows an account, that account can be reached from every source the interface's allowaccess admits.

remediation.summary: Give each administrator account a trusthost covering the management network only.

rules.notes: The factory trusthost is '0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0', which permits every source. An account is treated as restricted once at least one trusthost is narrower than that.

rules.title: Configure a login banner
rules.description: A banner should be shown before or immediately after authentication.
rules.rationale: In many jurisdictions an explicit notice is what makes access without authorisation actionable, and it removes any claim the system looked open to use.

remediation.summary: Turn on the pre-login banner and edit its text in the replacement message group.

rules.notes: Both banners default to 'disable', so a configuration that mentions neither shows no banner.

rules.title: Enforce a password minimum length of 8 or more
rules.description: A password policy should be enabled and should require at least eight characters.
rules.rationale: A short administrator password is guessable offline once a configuration backup or a hash leaks.

remediation.summary: Enable the password policy and set a minimum length.

rules.notes: 'set status enable' is what puts the policy in force. A password-policy block with 'set status disable' enforces nothing however long its minimum-length says.

rules.title: Configure at least one NTP server
rules.description: The device should synchronise its clock against a named time source.
rules.rationale: A log entry is only evidence if its timestamp can be correlated with every other device's, and an unsynchronised clock drifts far enough to break that within weeks.

remediation.summary: Point the device at your own NTP servers rather than the FortiGuard default.

rules.notes: A device left on 'set type fortiguard' is synchronised, but the configuration names no address, so this control reports NEEDS_REVIEW rather than passing or failing.

rules.title: Do not expose SNMP write access
rules.description: No reachable SNMP v1/v2c community should permit write operations.
rules.rationale: A read-write community is a cleartext password that reconfigures the device.

remediation.summary: Keep v1/v2c to queries and traps, and move any account that needs more to SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy.

rules.notes: The FortiOS SNMP agent serves v1/v2c queries and sends traps, and offers no community-scoped write, so a FortiOS community is read-only by construction rather than by configuration. The control is still evaluated so that a FortiOS report answers the same question as the Cisco and Junos reports.
